II17A-01.note: North-facing slopes are colder but have less UV, so darker beetles there separate heat from UV and favor Halloran. D (darker at high elevation) is the most tempting because it is true-looking, but the passage says both accounts fit the elevation pattern; A is the mirror that would favor Ide.

II17A-02.note: Clay is dug near the workshop, so Okrin-matching clay means the ware was made at Okrin. B is the tempting mirror but supports the trade account; D (matches both) is barely coherent and can be struck from the options alone.

II17A-03.note: Inland bridges get no sea spray, so more cracks in galvanized than ungalvanized bolts there isolate the acid-cleaning cause. B is the strongest distractor: galvanized bolts do crack more there, but they are coastal and the comparison bolts are inland, so salt spray could explain it.

II17A-04.note: To be younger than EVERY southern plain, Sorrin must have fewer craters than the least-cratered southern plain, Dunmo (57). C and D also compare Sorrin with southern plains but do not cover the binding case; A uses Kettle, a northern plain, which is irrelevant to the claim.

II17A-05.note: The 8-hour schedule (peak 16 < 20, trough 5.2 > 4) is the least frequent one inside both limits. B (12-hour) tempts as less frequent, but its peak of 21 exceeds the limit and its trough of 3.1 falls below it; A is within limits but not the least frequent.

II17A-06.note: The clay sits at 85 m, so P (22 m) is shallow and S (96 m) is deep. B is the strongest trap: it has the largest contrast, but R's 78 m screen is still above the clay, so both wells are shallow; C and D also compare two wells in the same aquifer.

II17B-01.note: The board heard only merchant-merchant cases, while the herring slump would cut borrowing for everyone, so a drop in merchant suits alone favors Calloway. A tempts, but the inland towns lacked both the board and the herring trade, so it does not separate the two causes; D favors the herring account.

II17B-02.note: The horns are used in both settings, but the veterans' pace matters only in processions, so equal slowing in seated concerts favors Lindqvist. B favors the archivist; D tempts as a timing argument but lines up with the archivist's 1919 date; C runs against the horns.

II17B-03.note: Hauling charges were set by weight, so cheaper hauling should narrow gaps most for heavy, low-value grain. A is the strong distractor, but the bulletin riders also used the turnpikes, so turnpike towns do not separate the accounts; B fits the bulletin account.

II17B-04.note: The claim is conditional on already having books, so the right comparison is books only (+8) against books and lessons (+9). C is true but only shows the effect of the books; A shows lessons help children without books, which is not the conclusion.

II17B-05.note: Submissions doubled while acceptances quadrupled, so the acceptance rate rose from 25% to 50%, which is Brassard's receptivity claim. C tempts but compares accepted counts across genres without any submissions, so it cannot show a rate; B gives only submissions, which fits the supply account.

II17B-06.note: The same people were 20-29 in 1995 and 45-54 in 2020, and their use held from 38% to 40%, so they kept the vowel as they aged. A is the strongest trap: it shows the change spreading but compares two different cohorts; B and D are cross-sectional age gaps, which the youthful-habit account also predicts.
